chunks: 1940 - And Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: 'I instruct the servant girl to look toward the dawn, and she says that it has not yet risen, so I eat. Then I look and find that it had already risen when she looked.'
He عليه السلام said: 'Make it up. However, if you had been the one who looked, there would have been nothing upon him.'

key_terms.الْجَارِيَةَ: a servant girl whose report about dawn was relied upon
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: the time of dawn marking the beginning of the fasting prohibition on eating
key_terms.اِقْضِهِ: make up that day of fasting
key_terms.شَيْءٌ: any liability or consequence in this context
key_terms.فَآكُلُ: I then eat, meaning eating on the basis of that information

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone eats before dawn in Ramadan after relying on another person who wrongly says fajr has not begun?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about eating at the end of the pre-dawn period in sawm (fasting) when one relies on another person's observation of fajr. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the fasted day must be made up if one ate based on another's mistaken report, while indicating that if the person had personally checked, there would be no liability.
